competitive_landscape: Access is mostly by Auric/Coastal Aviation light aircraft; the sea route to Dar es Salaam (~69.5nm) is served by slow boats and is rough and infrequent. There is no fast premium or zero-emission marine option.

demand_signals.label: Mainland sea link
demand_signals.note: Long, slow crossing ripe for a fast clean alternative

journeys.today: A long, rough slow-boat crossing or a light-aircraft charter.
journeys.with_navier: A fast, stable foiling sea link at the edge of Pioneer II range — a clean alternative to flying.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The ~69.5nm Mafia ↔ Dar crossing sits right at the Pioneer II 70nm range edge — a flagship long-haul electric leg, plus short in-park transfers around the marine reserve.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) comfortably covers Mafia ↔ Dar and opens Mafia ↔ Zanzibar as a routine single hop.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that clean foiling island mobility works for marine-park eco-luxury — transferable to Tanzania's protected islands.

regulatory_note: Operations centre on the Mafia Island Marine Park (Tanzania's first marine park); zero-wake, zero-emission foiling suits the protected reef and whale-shark waters. Engagement via the Marine Parks & Reserves Unit and SUMATRA/TASAC.
seasonality: Whale-shark season Oct–Mar; long rains Mar–May. The Mafia channel is exposed — foiling smooths the crossing in the windier months.

sources.label: Mafia Island Marine Park (Marine Parks & Reserves Tanzania)

summary: Mafia Island lies south of Zanzibar off the Tanzanian coast, anchored by the Mafia Island Marine Park and famous for seasonal whale-shark encounters. It is reached by small plane or a long sea crossing from Dar es Salaam; surface links are slow and weather-dependent.
tagline: Tanzania's quiet dive island — whale sharks, a marine park, and a long sea link to Dar.
